# Results — Study 867 (Currency Crash Risk)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen (2008): **high-carry currencies are exposed to crash
risk**, their returns are **negatively skewed** ("up by the stairs, down by the
elevator"), the higher the carry the deeper the skew, and a long-high / short-low carry
basket inherits that crash tail. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped), i.e. as-of 2026-06-30.
Fingerprint `ad1028e019f0` (weekly USD-per-foreign panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily FX spot (`auto_adjust=True`), **8 currencies vs USD** (EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, CAD, CHF, NZD, **MXN**), resampled to **weekly** (Friday last), 2003-12-12 → 2026-06-26, **1,177** weekly returns |
| Quote convention | every pair normalised to **USD-per-foreign-currency**: `EURUSD=X / GBPUSD=X / AUDUSD=X / NZDUSD=X` kept as-is; `JPY=X / CAD=X / CHF=X / MXN=X` are USD-base (foreign per USD) and **inverted** — so a rise always means the foreign currency appreciated vs the dollar |
| Carry | a fixed per-currency **carry proxy** = long-run average annualised short-rate differential vs USD (MXN +5.5, NZD +1.8, AUD +1.6 … JPY −1.6, CHF −1.4). True deposit/forward rates are not on yfinance — named a proxy; the crash verdict rests on the realized **skewness** off spot, only the carry *ordering* matters |
| Signal — basket | dollar-neutral **long top-3 / short bottom-3 carry** basket; its realized skewness (population third moment) with a **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** on the standardised-cubed-residual series `g=z³` (`mean(g)=skew`) |
| Signal — cross-section | each currency's own realized skewness regressed on its carry across the 8-name cross-section (slope, analytic *t*, Spearman rank correlation) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: carry ranking known at close `t` → held over `t+1` (static ranking makes it immaterial). The costed book charges 2 bps/side rebalance on the 2.0-NAV gross book + borrow on the short leg |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the basket skew and premium; a 2,000-relabeling **label-shuffle placebo** on the basket skew; a 20,000-draw permutation *p* on the Spearman rank correlation; a two-era cut; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The basket is a fixed **current** membership
(G10 + MXN), with no defunct or de-pegged legs (e.g. no pre-1999 EMS currencies), so the
magnitudes are an **upper bound** on a real-time, point-in-time currency universe.

## The headline — the carry basket's crash skew

Dollar-neutral long-top-3 / short-bottom-3 carry basket, weekly (n = **1,177** weeks):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **realized skewness** | **−1.39** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* on the skew | **−1.51** |
| premium | +6.33 bps/wk (**+3.29%/yr**), NW *t* = **+1.73**, Sharpe 0.34 |
| worst week / max drawdown | **−13.30%** / **−36.0%** |
| calm weeks vs worst-5% weeks (annualised) | **+12.6%/yr** vs **−173.6%/yr** |

The crash shape is **unmistakable and correctly signed**: the basket is deeply
negatively skewed (**−1.39**), with a single worst week of **−13.3%** (the Oct-2008
carry unwind) and a **−36%** peak-to-trough drawdown — exactly the "up by the stairs,
down by the elevator" tail Brunnermeier et al describe. The calm-week return (+12.6%/yr)
is handed back many times over in the worst 5% of weeks (−173.6%/yr annualised). **But**
the strict significance bar is not cleared: a Newey-West *t* on the basket's *own*
skewness is only **−1.51** — the skew *t*-statistic is inherently low-powered when the
asymmetry is driven by a handful of rare crashes (the synthetic control below shows a
planted skew of −3.5 still returns skew *t* ≈ −1.0). The economic signature is real; its
formal *t* is borderline.

## The skew-carry cross-section — does higher carry predict more negative skew?

Each currency's realized skewness regressed on its carry proxy (n = **8** currencies):

| currency (carry) | MXN (+5.5) | NZD (+1.8) | AUD (+1.6) | GBP (+0.4) | CAD (+0.2) | EUR (−0.4) | CHF (−1.4) | JPY (−1.6) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| realized skew | −1.19 | −0.35 | −1.18 | −0.63 | −0.43 | −0.11 | **+1.98** | +0.28 |

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope (skew on carry) | **−0.312** |
| analytic *t* on the slope | **−2.41** |
| R² | 0.49 |
| **Spearman rank correlation** | **−0.833** (permutation *p* = **0.008**) |
| high-carry leg skew vs low-carry leg skew | **−1.08** vs **+0.38** (diff **−1.46**) |

This is the **cleanest** part of the claim: the higher a currency's carry, the more
negative its realized skew, a **strongly monotone** relation (Spearman **−0.83**, only
0.8% of random rank orderings are this monotone). The two funding currencies (CHF, JPY)
carry the only *positive* skews — CHF's **+1.98** is the mirror image: the 2015 SNB
de-peg was a violent *upward* safe-haven spike, a crash *up* for the funding leg. The
high-carry long leg (MXN/NZD/AUD) is negatively skewed (−1.08) while the low-carry short
leg is positively skewed (+0.38) — the carry basket is short the crash on both sides.

## Placebo — is the negative skew tied to the carry ordering?

Shuffle which currency owns which carry value (2,000 relabelings), rebuild the basket,
remeasure its skew:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed basket skew | **−1.39** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.001 (0.815) |
| left-tail *p* | **0.0335** |

Only **3.4%** of random carry relabelings produce a basket this negatively skewed — the
crash tail is specifically tied to the **true carry ordering**, not a generic artefact of
these eight currencies.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2015-01-01)

| era | basket skew (NW *t*) | premium/yr (NW *t*) | skew-carry slope (*t*, Spearman) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2004-2014 (n=577) | **−1.41** (−1.21) | +3.70% (+1.19) | −0.227 (**−3.39**, −0.786) |
| 2015-2026 (n=600) | **−1.11** (−1.92) | +2.90% (+1.30) | −0.431 (−1.58, **−0.833**) |

The **sign is stable in both halves** — the basket is negatively skewed and the
skew-carry cross-section is strongly monotone (Spearman −0.79 / −0.83) throughout. But
the formal significance is **borderline and era-dependent**: the basket-skew NW *t* never
reaches −2 (−1.21 / −1.92), and the cross-sectional slope's *t* falls from −3.39 to −1.58
across the break (even as the rank monotonicity is undiminished). The effect is real in
sign and shape but does not clear the strict "robust |t| ≥ 2 in *both* eras" bar.

## The timer — can you get paid for the crash risk?

Costed carry book (2 bps/side rebalance + borrow on the short leg), n = **1,177** weeks:

| borrow (bps/yr) | gross | net | net Sharpe | *t* (net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | +3.29%/yr | **+1.21%/yr** | 0.13 | +0.64 |
| 25 | +3.29%/yr | +0.96%/yr | 0.10 | +0.50 |
| **50** | +3.29%/yr | **+0.71%/yr** | 0.07 | +0.37 |
| 100 | +3.29%/yr | +0.21%/yr | 0.02 | +0.11 |

The premium the crash is meant to compensate is **weak to begin with** (+3.29%/yr gross,
NW *t* = +1.73, not significant) and **collapses to +0.71%/yr** (Sharpe 0.07, *t* = 0.37)
at a modest 50 bps/yr borrow — all while a **−36%** drawdown and a **−13%** worst week sit
underneath. You are paid almost nothing to hold a deep negative crash tail: the textbook
picking-up-pennies-in-front-of-the-steamroller shape.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel: carries spread across the cross-section, a common risk-off
factor whose loading rises with carry, and a `edge` knob on the factor's fat negative
tail. No network.

| world | result |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge=0`), **20 seeds** | basket skew *t* mean **+0.02** (sd 0.73), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20**; skew-carry slope mean +0.0019 |
| planted (`edge=0.02`, seed 867) | basket skew **−3.50**; skew-carry slope **−0.696** (*t* = **−9.98**, Spearman **−0.976**) |

The powered detector — the **skew-carry slope** — recovers a planted carry-crash relation
cleanly (*t* = −9.98) and stays silent on the null (0/20 false fires). Note the basket
*skew t* stays ≈ −1.0 even at a planted skew of −3.5: the skewness *t*-statistic is
structurally low-powered against rare crashes, which is exactly why the real basket's
−1.39 skew shows only *t* = −1.51. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited
in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The Brunnermeier-Nagel-Pedersen crash-skew signature is **genuinely
  present and correctly signed**: the carry basket is deeply negatively skewed (**−1.39**,
  tied to the carry ordering, label-shuffle *p* = **0.034**), the skew-carry cross-section
  is strongly monotone (Spearman **−0.83**, permutation *p* = **0.008**) and stable in sign
  across both eras, and the crash accounting is textbook (worst week −13%, max DD −36%,
  worst-5% weeks −174%/yr). **But** the strict green bar — a robust Newey-West |t| ≥ 2 that
  holds across sub-eras — is **not cleared**: the conservative NW *t* on the basket's own
  skewness is only **−1.51** (−1.21 / −1.92 by era, the skew *t* being structurally
  low-powered against rare crashes), and the cross-sectional slope's *t* falls to −1.58 in
  the late era. Real in sign and shape, borderline in formal significance ⇒ **Weak**.
  *Survivorship: fixed current membership (no de-pegged legs) — magnitudes are an upper
  bound, named on the Signal axis.*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The premium the crash is supposed to pay for is weak to begin
  with (+3.29%/yr gross, NW *t* = +1.73) and collapses to **+0.71%/yr** (Sharpe 0.07,
  *t* = 0.37) at a modest 50 bps/yr borrow — you are paid almost nothing to carry a −36%
  drawdown and a −13% worst week. Picking up pennies in front of the steamroller.
